corrections_or_clarifications.verified_scope: The held-out set is not an unconditional random sample from the benchmark. It is conditioned on both recipient LLMs failing a preliminary seed-0 no-knowledge run, then 20 tasks are sampled from that failure intersection. This is a deliberately hard, selected evaluation set.

The paper states the seed-0 selection runs are separate from the three evaluation seeds, which avoids reusing the same random seed for selection and scoring. However, task inclusion is still conditioned on baseline failure, so absolute rates and effect sizes should not be generalized to the full benchmark distribution.

The positive deltas causally support the utility of the frozen donor asset plus the task-conditioned adapter under this transfer setup versus no knowledge. They do not isolate which internal knowledge-capture stage (task forum, cross-task forum, distillation) caused the benefit, nor do they establish that the asset alone without the adapter would produce the same gains.

Cross-family gains support portability beyond same-family use, but 'donor-agnostic structure' is an interpretation rather than a separately isolated causal variable. Preserve the exact observed cross-family cells and variance instead of upgrading this to a universal donor-agnostic claim.

The authors summarize the GPT-authored bundle as the stronger donor. Numerically this is strict in all ARC cells and the GPT-recipient Polyglot cell, but tied at 11.7±2.9 for the Haiku recipient on Polyglot. Downstream wording should use 'stronger or tied in the reported cells' if precision matters.

unresolved_gaps: Component-level ablations isolating task-level forum, cross-task forum, distillation, and task-conditioned adapter remain unresolved in this audit.
Independent numerical replication of the transfer matrix remains unresolved.
The exact candidate-pool sizes before failure-intersection filtering and robustness to alternative held-out selection rules were not established by the passages verified here.
